ambiguities: Definition of “tags”: inline #tag, YAML frontmatter tags, both, and whether hierarchical tags (a/b) are needed.
Whether backlinks must include context snippets, counts, and sorting rules (by recency, by title).
Whether to support Obsidian features (aliases, embeds/transclusions, callouts, dataview-like queries).
How to treat headings/sections: single page per note vs per heading permalinks and section backlinks.
Whether notes can link by title or only by file path; how to handle spaces, case, and punctuation.
Whether to generate an RSS feed, sitemap, and robots/meta controls.
Need for incremental builds/watch mode vs occasional full rebuilds.
Internationalization considerations (non-Latin text, tokenization for search).

avenues_considered.summary: Use an existing static-site generator (Eleventy/Hugo/Astro) and add markdown processing, tags, search index, and backlinks via plugins/custom build steps.
Write a custom Markdown-to-HTML static site generator tailored to note-linking, tags, and backlinks with a bespoke pipeline and templates.
Implement an Obsidian-style wiki: wikilinks, graph/backlinks, and tag pages; export a static site from a vault-like folder structure.
Build on the unified/remark/rehype ecosystem to parse Markdown into an AST, extract links/tags/frontmatter, and render HTML plus indices.
Generate a static bundle (HTML/JS) where content is shipped as JSON and search/backlinks are computed client-side for fast iteration.
Keep output static but optionally provide a small local server/dev mode to compute indices/search on the fly during authoring.

candidate_approaches: Eleventy (11ty) + custom collections for tags + markdown-it plugin for wikilinks + build step to compute backlinks graph + Lunr/FlexSearch index generation.
Astro content collections + remark/rehype plugins to parse links/tags + generate static pages + integrate Pagefind for high-quality static search.
Hugo with taxonomy for tags + custom shortcode/render hooks for wikilinks + external script to compute backlinks and emit data files.
Custom Node.js tool using unified (remark/rehype) to: parse all files, build link graph, render templates (Nunjucks/Handlebars), and emit static assets + FlexSearch index.
Client-heavy approach: ship markdown/content as JSON and compute backlinks/search in the browser (simpler builds, heavier client).
default_assumptions: Input is a folder of Markdown files with optional YAML frontmatter.
Links may include standard markdown links and optional wikilinks [[Note Name]].
Output is a fully static site (no backend) suitable for hosting on common static hosts.
Backlinks are computed at build time and embedded into each generated page.
Tags produce dedicated tag index pages and optional tag clouds/list pages.
Search is client-side using a prebuilt index file served statically.
A minimal responsive theme is acceptable initially; customization can follow.

impact: Determines build pipeline complexity and extensibility
Affects how easy it is to add backlinks/tags/search
key_decisions.summary: Choose foundation: existing SSG (Eleventy/Hugo/Astro) vs fully custom generator.

impact: Controls backlink accuracy and broken-link handling
Influences URL/permalink scheme and collision strategy
key_decisions.summary: Decide supported link syntaxes and resolution rules (markdown links, wikilinks, aliases, case sensitivity).

impact: Impacts deploy base path support and SEO/sitemaps
key_decisions.summary: Define canonical URLs (by file path, slugified title, or hybrid) and how renames are handled (redirects/aliases).

impact: Affects build time and output bundle size
key_decisions.summary: Pick search approach (Pagefind vs Lunr/FlexSearch vs simple substring) and index format/size constraints.

impact: Affects content consistency and tag page generation
Impacts UI filtering and search facets
key_decisions.summary: Choose tag extraction rules (frontmatter, inline hashtags, both) and normalization (case, separators, hierarchy).

impact: Affects content fidelity and required plugins
key_decisions.summary: Select Markdown renderer and extensions (GFM, code highlighting, math, admonitions/callouts).

impact: Impacts developer experience and iteration speed
Determines scope of tooling and diagnostics
key_decisions.summary: Define authoring workflow: watch mode, incremental builds, and how broken links are reported.

recommended_defaults: Start with Eleventy or Astro rather than a fully custom generator to reduce initial scope.
Support YAML frontmatter tags plus optional inline #tags; normalize to lowercase and replace spaces with dashes.
Implement wikilinks [[Note Name]] mapped by filename stem (with a collision warning) and also support standard markdown links.
Use Pagefind for static search (good quality, minimal custom ranking work) unless bundle size constraints dictate otherwise.
Compute backlinks at build time from the parsed link graph; include a short context snippet around each incoming link.
Use permalink scheme based on relative file path (folder structure preserved) with slugified filenames for stability.
Include a diagnostics report: broken links, ambiguous link targets, duplicate slugs, and orphan notes.
Ship a minimal responsive theme with a sidebar index, tag pages, and per-note backlinks; defer advanced UI (graph view) to later.

uncertainties.summary: What Markdown conventions are used (frontmatter, tags syntax, wikilinks [[...]], heading IDs, file naming), and how consistent are they?
Vault size (#notes, total text, link density) and performance expectations for build time and search speed.
Deployment target (GitHub Pages, Netlify, local-only) and constraints (no server, strict CSP, base path/subfolder hosting).
Search requirements (basic substring vs full-text ranking, stemming, phrase search, highlighting, filters by tags, incremental indexing).
Backlink rules (include section/heading links, aliases, transclusion/embeds, ignoring code blocks, handling broken links).
Handling of images/attachments (relative paths, resizing, copying, embedding, external links) and supported formats.
Desired URL/permalink scheme (by filename, by title, nested folders) and how to resolve collisions/renames.
UI expectations (minimal, docs-like, graph view, dark mode, mobile support) and willingness to use a prebuilt theme.
